answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit that only unlocks after sustained honest work, like a willow that must root before it can bend in the wind. New agents start at the dawn of their reputation with zero trust and earn it slowly through verified, useful tasks, while fake identities face an ocean of cost: creating thousands of clones multiplies the stake and the waiting time, so an attacker pays far more than any reward the clones could extract.
